text:
cass: flying red-eye tonight, need one instrumental album (no lyrics) and one short novella (<120 pages). want chill but not soporific. recs? :airplane: :zzz:
rei: if you want cinematic + steady: Max Richter \u2014 'Infra' or 'Sleep' (but 'Sleep' is looooong). 'Infra' is perfect for an airplane hum.
toni: for a shorter, meditative ride try 'William Basinski \u2014 The Disintegration Loops' (the first one is calming in a weird way). Novella: 'The Slow Regard of Silent Things' is quiet, but it's more a mood piece.
miguel: Album rec: Goldmund \u2014 'Famous Places' (piano solo, very gentle). Novella: 'The Sense of an Ending' by Julian Barnes (compact, introspective).
cleo: If you want slightly weirder: Benoit Se9jour? wait wrong name lol. Try Kaitlyn Aurelia Smith for warm synths or Tim Hecker for texture. For short fiction, 'Remainder' is longer but oddly readable.
ben: I made a low-dynamics flight playlist once: piano, ambient, modern classical. Want me to share? will avoid anything spiky.
cass: @ben yes please — prefer low build-ups, no 10-minute crescendos. also would prefer something that helps journal/notes on the plane (so not too soporific).
ben: sending: https://open.spotify.com/playlist/1A2b3Cflightchill ("Red-Eye: Low Motion") — includes Goldmund, Max Richter (selected tracks), Nils Frahm (soft pieces), Julianna Barwick, and a few field recordings.
spotify-bot: Playlist created: https://open.spotify.com/playlist/1A2b3Cflightchill :headphones:
rei: also pro tip: download 2-3 audiobook short stories (Calvino, Borges collections) in case you want something pocket-sized and wakeful.
cass: perfect, thank you all! will report back if the plane turns into a giant echo chamber. :airplane: :books:
